name: MYO5B-related Progressive Familial Intrahepatic Cholestasis

criteria.description: Identification of biallelic pathogenic variants in the MYO5B gene
Onset of intrahepatic cholestasis in infancy or early childhood with persistent pruritus
Exclusion of other known causes of progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis by clinical, biochemical, and genetic testing
Liver biopsy showing canalicular cholestasis with minimal inflammation and absence of ductopenia
Normal or low gamma-glutamyltransferase (GGT) levels despite cholestasis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of biallelic pathogenic MYO5B variants plus clinical evidence of early-onset intrahepatic cholestasis with exclusion of other PFIC types
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Liver biopsy and biochemical markers support diagnosis but are not definitive without genetic confirmation.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Persistent severe pruritus due to cholestasis
pathognomonic.notes: Intense itching often refractory to standard treatments
searchTerms: persistent itchy skin from liver problem

pathognomonic.notes: Elevated direct bilirubin indicating intrahepatic cholestasis

pathognomonic.symptomName: Normal or low serum gamma-glutamyltransferase (GGT) despite cholestasis
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic biochemical feature distinguishing from other cholestatic disorders
searchTerms: normal or low GGT despite bile blockage

common.notes: Poor weight gain and growth delay in infancy
Yellow discoloration of skin and sclera

common.symptomName: Fat-soluble vitamin deficiencies (A, D, E, K)
common.notes: Due to impaired bile acid secretion and absorption
searchTerms: lack of vitamins A, D, E, K
high bile acid levels in blood
scarring of liver progressing to cirrhosis

occasional.notes: Enlarged spleen secondary to portal hypertension
Elevated transaminases reflecting liver cell damage
searchTerms: liver cell damage from bile buildup

occasional.notes: Reported in some cases, possibly secondary to chronic illness

searchTerms: high blood pressure in portal vein
bleeding from enlarged veins in liver disease

rare.notes: Secondary skin lesions from chronic scratching

imaging: Ultrasound showing hepatomegaly and possible liver fibrosis
other: Liver biopsy demonstrating canalicular cholestasis with minimal inflammation and absence of ductopenia

distinguishingFeatures: Similar cholestasis but may have elevated GGT
Elevated bile salt export pump deficiency
Clinical overlap but distinct genetic cause
Abnormal bile acid profiles on biochemical testing
May respond to bile acid replacement therapy

redFlags: Early onset severe pruritus refractory to standard therapies
Progressive conjugated hyperbilirubinemia with normal GGT
Failure to thrive in infancy with hepatomegaly
references: Sambrotta M, Strautnieks S, Papouli E, et al. Mutations in MYO5B cause progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis type 6. Nat Commun. 2019;10(1):3350.
